correctness.rationale: Direct double integrals on a tree give exact first and second moments. The Schur–Ostrowski derivative quotients are 2(1-x-y) and 2[(x+y)(1-x-y)+R2] for the first and second raw moments, both positive for m>=3. For m=3 the variance quotient is 2z(1+12xyz)/3>0. Exact rational p,q have a strictly negative variance difference under strict majorization, and a continuity embedding extends this to all m>=4. The positive pairwise quotient at the uniform point rules out Schur-concavity. The included verifier executed 237 exact algebra/integral/majorization checks.

originality.rationale: Inspected closest accessible primary literature on continuous mean distance, vertex-distance majorization, and K-spider convex flows, as well as directly relevant public metric-star configuration-space and norm results. None supplies the second-moment formula plus sharp centered-variance majorization classification for arclength-uniform weighted star trees. The analogous four-petal flower result is not covering: cycles and trees have different shortest-path kernels. This is best-of-knowledge, not a claim of exhaustive global priority.

value.rationale: Complete natural threshold m=4 across every positive arm-length vector: it distinguishes mean/raw-square increase from the centered variance reversal while holding a one-hub tree topology fixed. Exact self-contained formulas and rational witness are informative for geometric-probability dispersion on transportation networks, beyond a routine normalization or a known-table recomputation. No downstream general theorem is necessary to make the sharp structural boundary worthwhile.
